title: Glioblastoma therapy with Serine- and Glycine-free diet (B-FREE) Trial
summary:
his study investigates how a special diet that excludes the two amino acids serine and glycine affects the body and the tumor in patients with a glioblastoma or another malignant brain tumor.

Participants follow a ten-day dietary program in which they consume only a specially prepared liquid formula that contains no serine or glycine. The goal is to find out whether this diet can influence the tumor’s metabolism and whether it is safe and well tolerated.

During the diet, blood and urine samples are taken at several time points, MRI scans of the brain are performed, and participants complete questionnaires on quality of life. Stool samples are also collected to examine possible changes in gut bacteria.

After completing the diet, participants undergo their planned tumor surgery or biopsy. The tumor tissue obtained during the procedure is analyzed in the laboratory to determine whether the diet has led to any metabolic or immune-related changes in the tumor.

The study aims to determine whether this type of dietary intervention is feasible, safe, and well tolerated, and whether it could serve as a potential complementary approach in the treatment of brain tumors in the future.

interventions.name: A total of 20 evaluable patients are to be enrolled in the study. Eligible participants are those with imaging findings suggestive of a malignant glioma or a recurrence of a previously diagnosed glioma, for whom an interdisciplinary tumor board has established the indication for biopsy or resection.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- suspicion of glioma WHO grade II, III or IV as assessed by cerebral imaging (MRI)
- interdisciplinary recommendation for resection or biopsy
- Karnofsky performance status >= 60, ECOG <= 2
- creatinine <= 2,0 mg/dl, urea <= 100 mg/dl
- ALAT, ASAT <= 7x upper normal limit
- INR ≤ 1,5, thrombocytes > 100000/µl, leukocytes > 3000/µl
Exclusion criteria:
- severe diarrhea, vomiting, malabsorption syndrome, bowel obstruction, subileus or active gastrointestinal bleeding. 
- insulin-dependent diabetes
- uncontrolled thyroid function
- pancreatic insufficiency
- decompensated heart failure (NYHA > 2)
- myocardial infarction within the last 6 months, symptomatic atrial fibrillation
- severe acute infection or clinically relevant immunosuppression (HIV infection, granulocytopenia <1000/ µl, lymphocytopenia <500/ µl
- malnutrition, cachexia (BMI <18)
- other medical conditions that might increase the risk of the dietary intervention
- Pregnant or lactating female patients 
- dementia or other clinically relevant alterations of the mental status which could impair the ability of the patient to apply to the diet or understand the informed consent of the study
- dexamethasone > 4mg/day
- major contraindications to MRI scanning (e.g. presence of implanted MRI-incompatible cardiac devices)
- participate in other intervention clinical trials (including drugs, nutritional supplements, medical devices, etc.) within the last 3 months 
- allergy to sample components
- use of other nutritional supplements that may affect the effectiveness of the study
- Patients with cognitive impairments or mental illnesses that are unable to comprehend the research content
- Patients with insufficcient proficiency in German language to provide informed consent or participate in study procedures
